prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Context: FAA NextGen aims to raise National Airspace System (NAS) capacity; en route weather causes ~70% of US delays. System: NASA Airspace Technology Demonstrations 3 (ATD-3), decision aids for weather-avoidance routing, TMI response and metering. Subset: NASA Dynamic Weather Routes (DWR), cruise phase, uses existing weather/airspace/traffic data; extends NASA Direct-To tool; constraints are polygons. Current system: FAA traffic managers set static Flow Constrained Areas (FCA) and Severe Weather Avoidance Plans (SWAP, aka Playbook routes) 2-8 h ahead; airline dispatchers file plans >=45 min before push-back; Collaborative Trajectory Options Program (CTOP) is strategic only; amendments are manual; crews use FMS and short-range weather radar. Gap: no automation flags expired constraints or savings. DWR: ground automation analyzing aircraft at/above 10,000 ft from radar track and flight plan updates; seeks time/fuel-saving weather-avoidance or wind-favorable direct-to corrections considering convective weather, traffic conflicts, sector congestion, Special Use Airspace (SUA) and FAA restrictions. Route runs from Maneuver Start Point (MSP; default 5 min ahead, or FL240 entry for climbing flights in Fort Worth Center, ZFW; draggable; snaps to fix within 10 nmi) to Return Capture Fix (RCF; last flight plan fix in ZFW ~200 nmi limit rectangle or before arrival STAR). Alternative is a historical limit polygon in NAS Constraint Evaluation and Notification Tool (NASCENT), the Future ATM Concept Evaluation Tool (FACET) version of DWR. If savings >= user minimum (default 5 min), the route is probed; 1-2 auxiliary waypoints (fix-radial-distance format, optional snap-to named fix) are added. Advisories go to a DWR flight list shown on the FAA traffic manager's or airline ATC coordinator's traffic display. The list shows user-responsible flights, sorted by savings; entries remain while the last trajectory update still has an advisory. Fields: flight ID (call sign), savings, city pair, aircraft type, RCF, waypoint count, and indicators: TR (minutes to traffic conflict), SC (yellow/red sector congestion), WX (weather), TMI 'R' (active Route TMI). User selects and modifies the route before clearing the aircraft. Fig 5 interface: Plan-view GUI shows current flight

New part:
U0104: The proposed ‘DWR’ advisory is shown as a dashed-white line.
U0105: The downstream ‘Capture fix’ used to compute the direct route, and the ‘Auxiliary waypoint’ used to find the route around convective weather polygons, are displayed as well.
U0106: Flights that have sufficient user-defined flight-time savings are displayed in the ‘DWR list’ on the top-left part of the big window.
U0107: Figure 5: DWR Route Display Auxiliary Waypoint Return Capture Fix Maneuver Start (SWAP Route) Point (MSP) The long window at the bottom shows the current flight plan route and DWR advisory, along with time- savings for various downstream fixes at left.
U0108: This is labeled as the ‘Capture fix menu & flying time savings’ in the figure.
U0109: The two windows on the right show the sector congestion for the current flight plan route (top) and the DWR advisory (bottom).
U0110: The corresponding sector congestion values (as red or yellow sectors) for those routes are shown within.
U0111: Red sectors are those where the congestion is caused by aircraft that are all currently airborne, while yellow sectors have proposed departure aircraft causing predicted congestion.
U0112: This allows DWR users to visualize proposed routes and modify them if necessary using point, click, and drag inputs.
U0113: Users can adjust the RCF, the number and position of auxiliary waypoints, and the MSP through interactive points, click, and drag actions if needed.
U0114: Metrics, including flight time savings (or delay), proximity to current and forecast weather, downstream sector congestion, traffic conflicts, and SUA conflicts, all update dynamically as the user modifies a proposed route.
U0115: Conflicts with weather or traffic cause DWR to dismiss a potential reroute (trial plan) and keep searching for another (see Figure 6).
U0116: Figure 6: Example of trial plan with weather and traffic conflicts that would prevent DWR from suggesting this route.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
